identity: Lorindor's berry woods and pearl shore pay their tolls twice: to netters in the woods at night and to mirefolk who count pearls that were never theirs.

quests.title: The Harvest Should Have a Song
quests.text: I count the harvest in baskets, but I know something is wrong when I cannot hear the birds. Defeat five Unlicensed Poachers after dark in the {name:berrywoods} {dir_of:r20_anchor_018:berrywoods}, where their nets have emptied the branches. A berrywood ought to offer more than fruit and silence.

quests.title: A Pearl for Every Basket
quests.text: The Toll Mirefolk at {name:fenhold} {dir_from_giver:fenhold} demand a pearl for every crate my carters carry. Defeat five of them, by day or night, and approach from the edge of the camp so they cannot all rush you together. At these rates, I shall soon be packing pearls and charging extra for the berries.

quests.title: Let the Ledgers Agree
quests.text: Some of those toll pearls reach Highcourt, and I would like our human neighbours to know what bought them. Travel to Highcourt and speak with Mariel Waybook about Lorindor's tolls; she keeps the road accounts there. Between her ledger and mine, we may find where an honest delivery becomes somebody else's profit.

quests.title: Berries Do Not Walk Away
quests.text: Merren Oakstamp says my crates arrive half empty, as though the berries have taken a stroll. Speak with her at Whitebridge Market Close in Whitebridge Shire about the missing deliveries. It is a long journey through the human lands; a mount will spare your feet for the work awaiting you.

quests.title: Close the Pearl Account
quests.text: All those stolen tolls pass through the hands of {name:pearl_counter_iss} at the {name:pearl_camp} {dir_from_giver:pearl_camp}. Defeat four Toll Mirefolk there and then Iss, by day or night. I have checked the accounts twice: we owe them nothing, and our carters deserve to travel without paying for that conclusion.

quests.title: Accounts on the Border
quests.text: With Iss gone, Lorindor's accounts balance for the first time in a season, and it is time you kept accounts somewhere harder. Toren Waterbarrel at Cinderline Watch in Ashenward March feeds a garrison on the contested border and could use someone who counts as carefully as you fight. Follow the road out of Lorindor into the march, and finish your training first; the Accord's seal grows thin there.

quests.title: Do Not Follow That Light
quests.text: A traveller sees a light between the trunks and thinks someone has left a lantern for them. Extinguish five Wandering Wisps after dark in the {name:elderwood}, which lies {zone_area:elderwood}, before that kindness turns into another lost traveller. They appear only at night; keep the path in sight while you work.

quests.title: Give the Old Roots a Brace
quests.text: These roots held the earth before anyone thought to call us the Accord; I mean to repay the favour. Alloy iron with coal and bring me four Steel Bars here at the cutting for the props. Check your pick before seeking the deeper seams: respect for stone begins with the right tool.

quests.title: A Rootscribe Recommends You
quests.text: Kelda Screesort at Tarncut Mine in Frostbarrow Shelf knows what stone will bear, and I value her judgment. Make the journey to her and say I sent you to help with her work. She will probably ask whether I have measured anything properly yet; tell her the roots remain entirely satisfied.

quests.title: Optional: Passage at Ankle Height
quests.text: The Barnacle Pinchers on the {name:shell_strand} {dir_from_giver:shell_strand} have made our daytime shore patrol a rather undignified dance. Kill five by day so the wardens can walk their rounds. Leave the Bank Crabs alone; they have kept their side of the peace.

quests.title: Optional: A Light Between Every Root
quests.text: Among the {name:paleroots}, which lie {zone_area:paleroots}, Wandering Wisps make every gap look like a welcoming doorway. Extinguish six at night. I would rather our travellers find their way by the stars than trust anything so eager to lead them astray.

quests.title: Optional: What the Bark Cannot Bear
quests.text: The Moss-Antler Stags are stripping bark faster than the roots can mend, and affection alone will not save the trees. Cull six by day in the {name:paleroots}, which lie {zone_area:paleroots}. Their yellow names mean they will not attack first; choose your quarry, and take no more than I ask.

quests.title: Bounty: Keep a Song in the Branches
quests.text: The Unlicensed Poachers return to the {name:berrywoods} {dir_of:r20_anchor_018:berrywoods} whenever they think we have stopped listening. Defeat six after dark and return to me for Berrycourt's payment. This bounty remains available for further hunts; I intend to hear birds here next harvest too.

quests.title: Bounty: The Wardens' Night Watch
quests.text: We cannot leave a lamp beside every traveller, but we can put out the lights that deceive them. Extinguish six Wandering Wisps at night in the {name:elderwood} and return for the Wardenry's payment. Further watches carry the same bounty.

quests.title: Bounty: A Little Help for Old Roots
quests.text: Even roots that have held for centuries appreciate a brace before they need it. Bring me four Steel Bars here at the cutting for payment; this is a standing order you may fill again. I would rather replace a prop than write a song about the tunnel it failed to hold.
